Live: 31 of 33, 45 (43 distinct), 1 of 2, committed three times, 22. findings.item: TWO MECHANISMS IN O15 ARE PINNED BY NOTHING, and the header claims 'EVERY MECHANISM BELOW IS SEEN TO FAIL'
findings.detail: I re-ran the mutation sweep independently, one deletion at a time against the whole file, with the 70 self-test cases as the only judge. (A) THE ENV-NAME PAIRING ON THE DIRECT-READ ARM of shape one is unpinned. Replacing `if field is not None and f"{prefix}_{field.upper()}" in said:` with `if field is not None:` leaves SELF GREEN. The existing case _O15_NAMES_ANOTHER_LEVER pins only the BINDS arm, because its guard reads a LOCAL (`frac = float(mem.frac)`). I built the case that pins the other arm and drove it both ways: a function whose guard is `if float(mem.frac) < 0.0:` and whose raise says `f"MEM_QUOTA={quota}: ..."` is correctly SILENT today, and with that one condition removed O15 FAILS with a pre-emption finding against MEM_FRAC -- a lever the refusal message does not name. (B) THE REBIND-TO-A-DIFFERENT-FIELD HALF of _o15_bindings' kill is unpinned. Replacing `if field is None or (name in binds and binds[name] != field):` with `if field is None:` leaves SELF GREEN; the existing case _O15_REBOUND only exercises the `field is None` half (`frac = 0.0`). Driven: a function with `x = float(mem.frac)` / `if x < 0.0: raise ValueError(f"MEM_OTHER={x}: a negative share.")` / `x = float(mem.other)` is correctly SILENT today and produces a FALSE pre-emption finding against MEM_OTHER with that half removed. Both of these are INVENT-A-FINDING directions, which the header calls 'the one way this arm could invent a finding'. (C) separately, `if lit is None: return params, None` in _o15_config_params cannot be pinned by any case because it is behaviourally redundant: falling through adds None to `prefixes`, and the `len(prefixes) == 1` test below returns None in every reachable combination. Disabling it leaves SELF green and changes no verdict. So of the thirteen mechanisms the header says were 'deleted one at a time ... and the self-test went RED on all thirteen', at least two arms are not covered and one cannot be. The other eleven I drove -- M1 raise requirement, M2 Compare arm, M3 abstention gate, M4 kill-on-rebind (the `field is None` half), M5 bool rejection, M6 table holder, M7 O14 literal test, M8a env-name pairing (binds arm), M9 bounded-both-ends, M10 mislabelled-table abstention, M11b two-owner abstention, M13 Not/complement -- ALL go SELF-RED, and M12 (O14's visible-pair test) raises rather than passing, so it is pinned by control flow.

findings.item: O15's interval algebra is correct -- 20,000 random cases verified against dense sampling, plus 15 guard shapes against Python's own evaluation
findings.detail: This is the engine every O15 verdict rests on and nothing in the self-test tests it directly. I property-tested _o15_norm, _o15_complement, _o15_inter and _o15_union over 20,000 random pairs of span lists with endpoints on a half-integer grid (plus -inf/+inf) and both closedness flags, checking membership at 15 sample points chosen to land ON the endpoints: 0 violations of norm-preserves-membership, complement-inverts-membership, inter, union, and the disjoint-and-ascending invariant on every returned list. Separately I evaluated _o15_test_set against Python itself for 15 guard shapes -- `x < 0.0`, `x <= 0.0`, `x > 1.0`, `x >= 1.0`, `not 0.0 <= x <= 1.0`, `not 0.0 <= x < 1.0`, `0.0 <= x <= 1.0`, `x < 0.0 or x > 1.0`, `x != 0.0`, `x == 1.0`, `not (x < 0.0 or x > 2.0)`, `0.0 < x < 1.0`, `1.0 > x` (reversed operand order), `not x >= 0.0`, `x < 0.0 and x > -1.0` -- at 18 points each including -0.0, 1e-09, 0.9999999999999999 and 1.0000000000000002: 0 mismatches, 0 spurious abstentions.
